messages:
Rafa (CEO): opening a quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands. throw short, concrete Qs about mission/positioning and we'll answer.
Noah - Head of Product: quick clarity  our public top-line is 'inference platform' or 'inference runtime + tooling'?
Rafa (CEO): short answer: both. top-line = 'inference platform' but lead with runtime + tooling in technical collateral.
Leah (Strategy): how explicit should we be about 'not a model vendor'? some customers worry we'll lock them in.
Rafa (CEO): be explicit about portability. language: 'model-agnostic serving, bring-your-model or choose ours.' emphasize portability and exportable configs.
Omar (Sales): competitive play  vs big cloud endpoints during discovery? SDRs need a 15s reply.
Noah - Head of Product: "Cloud endpoints give model access; Redwood guarantees production-grade latency, controls, and unit economics."
Kai (Eng): product question  smart routing is mature enough to be on sales decks?
Noah - Head of Product: yes, include it as a differentiator but note GA features (routing, fallback) vs experiments (multi-az auto-failover).
Leah (Strategy): can we get a one-line metric to highlight externally?
Rafa (CEO): use 'median 99p latency for common workloads' + 'unit cost per 1k tokens' as headline comparables.
Omar (Sales): request: a private battlecard vs cloud providers that sales can use in calls.
Rafa (CEO): agreed. Marketing + Sales, produce a privacy-labeled battlecard. owner: Omar.
Kai (Eng): small ops ask: publish a clear fallback matrix so customers can plan UX degradation.
Noah - Head of Product: on it, will ship a short doc and a Console mock.
Rafa (CEO): thanks all. keep follow-ups short here. ops-bot logged task "battlecard + fallback doc" assigned to Omar; due 2026-04-06.
